day_shape: 91 items dominated by the digitally signed US-Iran MoU (Geneva signing Friday, Strait of Hormuz reopening, reported $300bn investment proposal), E4+ leaders' statement and UN Secretary-General welcome, IDF confirmation of a cancelled major Iran strike, continued Hezbollah-IDF exchanges in south Lebanon, and Iran executing two over Shahroud December unrest.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU signed digitally, Geneva Friday
threads.summary: The US said Trump, Vance and Iran's Ghalibaf digitally signed an MoU on Sunday, with formal signing set for Geneva on Friday and Trump saying the Strait of Hormuz will be 'completely opened' that day. Reports cite a possible $300bn investment fund tied to sanctions relief, while CIA Director Ratcliffe reportedly cast doubt on Iranian concessions and Vance said details remain unresolved.

threads.label: International and Israeli reactions to the deal
threads.summary: A joint E4+ leaders' statement from the UK, France, Germany and 14 other governments backed the US-Iran peace deal, and UN Secretary-General Guterres welcomed it. Netanyahu avoided criticising the agreement while IDF and Mossad officials called it insufficient; Bennett, Dermer and US Jewish groups voiced concern, and markets rose with oil down over $4 a barrel.

threads.label: Iranian regime framing of war's end
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted messages calling the enemy's plan after the imposed war 'blind', while IRIB carried Foreign Minister Araghchi saying war formally ended Monday and talks finalise Friday, with new rounds in Switzerland. Defa Press and IRIB quoted military and parliamentary figures claiming the US and Israel achieved none of their objectives; Iran International reported the digitally signed MoU split Tehran's political spectrum.

threads.label: IDF confirms cancelled major Iran strike
threads.summary: Israeli Air Force chief Maj. Gen. Omer Tischler told troops in a missive that a planned large wave of strikes on Iran was called off last week during the recent fighting. The Jerusalem Post reported Israeli satellites photographed Iran roughly 50,000 times during Operation Roaring Lion, and Channel 14 criticised US envoys Kushner and Witkoff's handling of the deal.

threads.label: Hezbollah-IDF exchanges in south Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah fired rockets, an anti-tank missile and mortars at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon Monday with no casualties, intercepting several projectiles and striking operatives in response. Lebanese media reported one killed in an Israeli drone strike on a car in Kfar Tebnit; Iran's Araghchi said any further Israeli attack on Lebanon would breach the understanding.

threads.label: Shahroud executions and internal repression
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press reported the Semnan judiciary executed Javad Zamani and Abolfazl Saaedi over the December 1404 Shahroud unrest on moharebeh and corruption-on-earth charges. The Jerusalem Post separately reported three femicide cases in Iran in one week described by regime outlets as 'familial disputes', and Iran International said New Zealand's Deputy PM David Seymour is considering an IRGC terrorist designation.

threads.label: Iran at the World Cup in Los Angeles
threads.summary: Iran drew 2-2 with New Zealand at Los Angeles Stadium in their World Cup opener, with boos, cheers and diaspora protests against Tehran's government. IRIB reported delays for Mehdi Taremi and Saeid Alhosseini at LAX caused the team to arrive at Tehkonda camp at 01:30 local time.

events.title_en: Air force intercepted several shells fired by terrorist Hezbollah towards the area where IDF forces operate in southern Lebanon
events.summary_en: Air force recently intercepted several shells fired by terrorist Hezbollah towards the area where IDF forces operate in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah also, in several separate incidents that occurred earlier today (Monday), fired an anti-tank missile and a number of mortar shells towards IDF forces operating in southern Lebanon, without causing casualties. IDF forces also identified, in four separate incidents during the day, a number of terrorists who were moving through vehicles and approached the forces in a manner that posed an immediate threat to them, whereupon the air force, under direction from field forces, attacked all threats precisely and in a targeted manner. The IDF will continue to work to remove any immediate threat.

events.title: The IDF says it struck and killed two Hamas operatives who posed a threat to troops in the Gaza Strip earlier today. A strike in central Gaza killed Saleh Khalifa, a cell commander in Hamas's Nuseirat Battalion, and strike in the Strip's north killed Muhammad al-Habil, a cell commander in Hamas's West Jabalia Battalion, according to the military. The IDF says the pair had been planning attacks on troops, "posed an imminent threat," and were then killed in "precise strikes."
